title: Bedrock streaming exception frames must raise HTTPException with a mapped status
answers: Bedrock stream throttling shows as 502 in client error chunk
gateway SSE error for Bedrock ThrottlingException has wrong status
Bedrock stream mid-response error status code
modelTimeoutException on Claude Bedrock stream reported as generic error
body:
Symptom: a Bedrock Claude stream that fails after it has started reports a generic error, so a client cannot tell throttling (429) from service unavailable (503) or timeout (408).
Root cause: `mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py:_event_stream_to_anthropic_sse` reads non-`event` frames; before the fix there was no status mapping.
Fix pattern: map `:exception-type` through `_BEDROCK_STREAM_EXCEPTION_STATUS` (429, 503, 408) with 502 as the default, and raise `HTTPException` so `safe_stream` writes that status into the SSE error chunk, the same way `send_stream_request` reports pre-first-frame errors.
Constraints: the mapping is only for the retryable frames listed; other exception frames map to 502. Decode frames with botocore `EventStreamBuffer` from `botocore.eventstream`, and keep the install hint for a missing boto3.
applies: Changes to the Bedrock event-stream to SSE conversion or to how stream errors are surfaced to clients.
says: Mid-stream errors from Bedrock report generic gateway failures instead of rate limits.
Streaming chat responses return generic 502 errors when Bedrock models time out.
Surface rate throttling as 429 status in streaming error events from Bedrock.
Client applications cannot distinguish service unavailability from timeouts during live model streams.
Map upstream provider exception types to specific HTTP codes inside stream chunks.
search: Bedrock streaming exception frames must map into specific HTTP status codes when raised as HTTP exceptions for server-sent events. In mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py:_event_stream_to_anthropic_sse, non-event frames have their :exception-type mapped via _BEDROCK_STREAM_EXCEPTION_STATUS to 429, 503, or 408, defaulting to 502. Raising HTTPException allows safe_stream to embed the mapped status code into the SSE error chunk, decoding frames via botocore EventStreamBuffer and preserving the missing boto3 install hint.
